pages.text: "One more!" Dari added a shell to his tower on the shore rocks. Autumn wind shook it; it was already nose-high. "As high as the lighthouse!"
Kkiruk fluttered down from the roof. The wing gust toppled the tower! Shells rolled below the rocks. Dari reared up and shouted. "I hate you! Go away!"
Startled, Kkiruk flew away. Dari pounded the rock with his flippers, scattering the remaining shells. Alone, he let his tail lie limp.
Mom came from the kitchen and sat beside him. "Something hot rushed up in your heart?" Dari sniffled and nodded. "That's an anger wave. Waves come, then go out again."
"How does it go out?" Dari asked. Mom rested a flipper on his tummy. "Breathe in through your nose—tummy out! Breathe out—let the wave go. See the sea waves come and go? Anger's like that."
"Together. One, breathe in." Dari's tummy rounded. "Two, breathe out..." His tummy settled. Mom smiled. "Feeling angry? Breathe out!"
Dari looked up at Kkiruk on the roof. "Sorry I shouted. I got angry all at once." He slapped his tail. Feeling angry? Breathe out!
Kkiruk fluttered down and sat close. "Sorry, sorry!" they repeated. With a wing, Kkiruk gently gathered scattered shells. Dari laughed. Laughter returned to the rocks.
They rebuilt the tower. This time, a wave washed it away! Anger stirred again, but Dari quickly put a flipper on his tummy. "One, breathe in! Two, breathe out! Three, we can build again!"
Mom stroked his back. "You sent the anger wave away. Wonderful!" Feeling angry wasn't bad; a big breath helped it ebb like a wave. "Feeling angry? Breathe out!" Dari smiled in Mom's arms.
